title.zh: 卷一百四十一 列傳第二十八: 太不花 察罕帖木兒
title.raw: 卷一百四十一 列傳第二十八: 太不花 察罕帖木兒 Volume 141 Biographies 28: Taibuhua, Chaghan Temur

sentences.zh: 太不花

translations.literal: Taibuhua
translations.idiomatic: Taibuhua

sentences.zh: 太不花，弘吉剌氏。

translations.literal: Taibuhua was of the Hongjila clan.
translations.idiomatic: Taibuhua belonged to the Hongjila clan.

sentences.zh: 世為外戚，官最貴顯。

translations.literal: For generations his family had been imperial affines, and their offices were the most exalted.
translations.idiomatic: His family had for generations been consorts of the imperial house, holding the most distinguished offices at court.

sentences.zh: 太不花沉厚有大度，以世冑入官，累遷雲南行省右丞，歷通政使、上都留守、遼陽行省平章政事。

translations.literal: Taibuhua was deep and steady, with great breadth of mind. Entering office through his noble lineage, he was repeatedly promoted to Right Chancellor of the Yunnan Branch Secretariat, and served in turn as Commissioner of the Bureau of Transmission, Urgent Commissioner of the Upper Capital, and Grand Councillor of the Liaoyang Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Deep and steady, with a generous temperament, Taibuhua entered government by virtue of his birth. He rose through the ranks to become Right Chancellor of the Yunnan branch secretariat, and later served as transmission commissioner, urgent commissioner of the Upper Capital, and grand councillor of the Liaoyang branch secretariat.

sentences.zh: 至正八年，太平為丞相，力荐太不花可大用，召入，為中書平章政事。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Zhizheng, Taiping became chancellor and strongly recommended that Taibuhua could be greatly employed. Taibuhua was summoned in and made Grand Councillor of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Zhizheng (1348), when Taiping became chancellor, he strongly urged that Taibuhua be given high responsibility. Taibuhua was summoned to court and appointed grand councillor of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 明年，太平既罷，脫脫復為相。

translations.literal: The next year Taiping was already dismissed, and Toghto again became chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Taiping was removed from office, and Toghto returned as chancellor.

sentences.zh: 太不花因黨於脫脫謀欲害太平，眾由是不​​平之。

translations.literal: Taibuhua, because he sided with Toghto, plotted to harm Taiping, and the multitude for this reason were displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Taibuhua aligned himself with Toghto and plotted against Taiping, and public opinion turned against him.

sentences.zh: 十二年，盜起河南，知樞密院事老章出師久無功，詔拜太不花河南行省平章政事，加太尉，將兵往代之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year bandits rose in Henan. The Privy Council Vice-Director Laozhang had led troops out for a long time without success. An edict appointed Taibuhua Grand Councillor of the Henan Branch Secretariat, with the additional title of Grand Marshal, to lead troops and replace him.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year (1352) rebels broke out in Henan. Privy Council vice-director Laozhang had campaigned for months without success. The court appointed Taibuhua grand councillor of the Henan branch secretariat and grand marshal, sending him with an army to relieve Laozhang.

sentences.zh: 未期月，平南陽、汝寧、唐、隨，又下安陸、德安等路，招降服叛，動合事宜，軍聲大振。

translations.literal: Before a full month had passed he pacified Nanyang, Runing, Tang, and Sui, and also took Anlu, De'an, and other circuits. He recruited surrender, subdued rebellion, and his actions at every turn fit the occasion; the army's renown greatly swelled.
translations.idiomatic: Within less than a month he pacified Nanyang, Runing, Tang, and Sui, then captured Anlu, De'an, and other circuits. Whether accepting surrenders or crushing revolts, his moves were always apt, and his army's reputation soared.

sentences.zh: 十四年，脫脫以太師、右丞相總大兵徵高郵，尋詔奪其兵柄，而升太不花本省左丞相，與太尉月闊察兒、樞密知院雪雪代總其兵。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year Toghto, as Grand Preceptor and Right Chancellor, commanded the great army to campaign against Gaoyou. Soon an edict stripped him of military authority, and Taibuhua was promoted to Left Chancellor of the same province, he together with Grand Marshal Yuekuochá'er and Privy Council Vice-Director Xuexue replacing him in overall command of the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year (1354) Toghto, as grand preceptor and right chancellor, took command of a great expedition against Gaoyou. Soon afterward an edict stripped him of his army. Taibuhua was promoted to left chancellor of the same province, and together with Grand Marshal Yuekuochá'er and privy council vice-director Xuexue he assumed overall command in Toghto's place.

sentences.zh: 山東、河北諸軍悉令太不花節制。

translations.literal: All armies of Shandong and Hebei were entirely placed under Taibuhua's command and control.
translations.idiomatic: All forces in Shandong and Hebei were placed under his command.

sentences.zh: 而太不花乃以軍士乏糧之故，頗驕傲不遵朝廷命令，軍士又往往剽掠為民患。

translations.literal: But Taibuhua, on the pretext that the soldiers lacked grain, was quite arrogant and did not obey the court's orders, and the soldiers also often plundered, becoming a calamity for the people.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Taibuhua, citing shortages of rations for his troops, grew arrogant and defied court orders, while his men frequently plundered the countryside and terrorized the populace.

sentences.zh: 十五年，監察御史也裡忽都等劾其慢功虐民之罪，於是天子下詔盡奪其職，俾率領火赤溫，從平章政事答失八都魯徵進。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year Supervising Censor Yelihudu and others impeached him for the crimes of slackening in duty and maltreating the people. Thereupon the Son of Heaven issued an edict stripping him of all his offices, ordering him to lead the Huochiwen and follow Grand Councillor Däshibadu'er on the advance campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year (1355) supervising censors including Yelihudu impeached him for neglecting his duties and abusing the people. The emperor then stripped him of all his posts by edict and ordered him to lead the Huochiwen auxiliaries in support of Grand Councillor Däshibadu'er's advance.

sentences.zh: 頃之，復拜湖廣行省左丞相，節制湖廣、荊襄諸軍，招捕沔陽、湖廣等處水陸賊徒。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was again appointed Left Chancellor of the Huguang Branch Secretariat, controlling the armies of Huguang and Jingxiang, to recruit and capture the water and land bandits of Mianyang, Huguang, and other places.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was reappointed left chancellor of the Huguang branch secretariat, with command over the Huguang and Jingxiang armies and orders to suppress bandits by land and water in Mianyang, Huguang, and neighboring regions.

sentences.zh: 會朝廷復拜太平為中書左丞相，太不花聞之，意不能平，歎曰：「我不負朝廷，朝廷負我矣。

translations.literal: It happened that the court again appointed Taiping Left Chancellor of the Central Secretariat. When Taibuhua heard this, his mind could not be at peace, and he sighed, saying, "I have not failed the court; the court has failed me.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the court reappointed Taiping as left chancellor of the Central Secretariat. When Taibuhua heard the news, he could not contain his resentment and sighed, "I have not failed the court—the court has failed me.

sentences.zh: 太平漢人，今乃復居中用事，安受逸樂，我反在外勤苦邪！」

translations.literal: Taiping is a Han man; now he again holds the center and wields power, comfortably receiving ease and pleasure, while I am instead outside enduring toil and hardship!"
translations.idiomatic: Taiping is a Han Chinese—yet he is back at the center wielding power, enjoying ease and comfort, while I am left to toil in the field!"

sentences.zh: 及擊賊，賊且退，諸將皆欲乘勝渡江，而太不花乃反勒兵而退，以養銳為名。

translations.literal: When they attacked the bandits and the bandits were about to retreat, all the generals wished to cross the river on the momentum of victory, but Taibuhua instead reined in the army and withdrew, under the name of resting the troops' sharpness.
translations.idiomatic: When they engaged the rebels and the enemy was on the verge of retreat, every general wanted to press the advantage and cross the river—but Taibuhua ordered a withdrawal, claiming he was conserving his troops' strength.

sentences.zh: 其後賊犯汴梁，守臣請援兵，至十往反，太不花乃始率兵援汴梁，而猶按甲不進。

translations.literal: Afterward the bandits attacked Bianliang. The defending officials requested relief troops, and only after ten round trips did Taibuhua at last lead troops to relieve Bianliang, yet he still held his armor and did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the rebels threatened Bianliang, the defenders pleaded for reinforcements again and again—ten times in all—before Taibuhua finally marched to their aid, and even then he held his army back without engaging.

sentences.zh: 時睢、亳、太康俱已陷，邊警日急。

translations.literal: At that time Sui, Bo, and Taikang had all fallen, and frontier alarms grew daily more urgent.
translations.idiomatic: By then Sui, Bo, and Taikang had all fallen, and the frontier alarms grew more urgent by the day.

sentences.zh: 或諫之曰：「賊旦夕且至，丞相兵不進何也？」

translations.literal: Someone admonished him, saying, "The bandits will arrive any day now—why does the Chancellor's army not advance?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone urged him, saying, "The rebels will be here any day—why does your army not advance?"

sentences.zh: 太不花顧左右大言曰：「我在，何物小寇敢犯境邪？

translations.literal: Taibuhua looked to those at his side and spoke loudly, saying, "While I am here, what trifling bandits would dare violate the borders?
translations.idiomatic: Taibuhua turned to his attendants and declared loudly, "As long as I am here, what petty raiders would dare cross our borders?

sentences.zh: 若等毋多言，我自有神算也。」

translations.literal: You people need not speak much; I myself have divine calculations."
translations.idiomatic: Say no more—I have my own stratagems."

sentences.zh: 既而縱軍出掠，百里之內，蕩然無遺。

translations.literal: Thereupon he let the army go out to plunder, and within a hundred li nothing was left.
translations.idiomatic: He then let his troops loose to plunder, and for a hundred li around nothing was left standing.

sentences.zh: 繼又渡師河北，聲取曹、濮，遂駐於彰德、衛輝。

translations.literal: Next he again crossed the army to Hebei north of the river, proclaiming that he would take Cao and Pu, and then encamped at Zhangde and Weihui.
translations.idiomatic: He next crossed into Hebei, announcing an attack on Cao and Pu, then halted his army at Zhangde and Weihui.

sentences.zh: 俄而曹、濮之賊奪竄晉、冀，大同亦相繼不守，遂蔓延不可製。

translations.literal: Before long the bandits of Cao and Pu seized and fled into Jin and Ji; Datong also in succession could not be held, and the disorder spread until it could not be controlled.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the rebels of Cao and Pu swept into Shanxi and Hebei; Datong fell in turn, and the uprising spread beyond control.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以為憂，兩遣重臣諭以密旨，授之成算，而太不花恬不為意。

translations.literal: The court regarded this with anxiety and twice sent high ministers to instruct him with secret edicts and confer on him settled plans, yet Taibuhua was placidly unconcerned.
translations.idiomatic: The court was deeply alarmed and twice dispatched senior officials with secret instructions and a settled plan of campaign—but Taibuhua remained indifferent.

sentences.zh: 是時，其子壽童以同知樞密院事將兵分討山東，久無功，嘗以事入奏，語言有驕慢意，帝由是惡之。

translations.literal: At this time his son Shoutong, as Associate Director of the Privy Council, led troops in separate operations against Shandong. For a long time there was no success. He once entered to report on affairs, and his words had an air of arrogance and disrespect; the Emperor for this reason came to detest him.
translations.idiomatic: At this time his son Shoutong, serving as associate privy council director, led troops in a separate campaign in Shandong but achieved nothing for months. When he reported to court, his tone was arrogant, and the emperor took a dislike to him.

sentences.zh: 十八年，山東賊愈充斥，且逼近京畿，於是詔拜太不花中書右丞相，總其兵討山東。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year the bandits in Shandong grew ever more widespread and even drew near the capital region. Thereupon an edict appointed Taibuhua Right Chancellor of the Central Secretariat to command the troops in suppressing Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year (1358) the Shandong rebels grew bolder and pressed toward the capital. The court appointed Taibuhua right chancellor of the Central Secretariat and gave him overall command of the campaign in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 既渡河，即上疏以謂：「賊勢張甚，軍行宜以糧餉為先。

translations.literal: Once he had crossed the river, he at once submitted a memorial stating, "The bandits' momentum is greatly swollen; in military operations provisions should come first.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as he crossed the river, he memorialized the throne: "The rebels' strength is formidable; on campaign, supplies must come first.

sentences.zh: 昔漢韓信行軍，蕭何饋糧，方今措畫，無如丞相太平者，如令太平至軍中供給，事乃可濟，不然兵不能進矣。」

translations.literal: In former times when Han Xin marched, Xiao He supplied grain. For planning at present there is no one like Chancellor Taiping; if Taiping were ordered to come to the army to provide supplies, the affair could then succeed—otherwise the army cannot advance."
translations.idiomatic: When Han Xin campaigned, Xiao He fed his army. For organizing supplies today, no one equals Chancellor Taiping. If he were sent to the front to provision the troops, the campaign could succeed; otherwise the army cannot move."

sentences.zh: 其意實銜太平，欲其至軍中即害之也。

translations.literal: His real intent was that he bore a grudge against Taiping and wished that when Taiping came to the army he would at once be killed.
translations.idiomatic: In truth he nursed a grudge against Taiping and intended to kill him once he arrived at camp.

sentences.zh: 時參知政事卜顏帖木兒、張晉等分省山東，二人者嘗劾壽童不進兵，太不花至，則以其饋運不前斷遣之。

translations.literal: At that time the Vice Grand Councillors Buyan Temür, Zhang Jin, and others were provincial commissioners in Shandong. The two of them had once impeached Shoutong for not advancing the army. When Taibuhua arrived, he cut them off and dismissed them on the charge that their transport of supplies did not go forward.
translations.idiomatic: Vice grand councillors Buyan Temür and Zhang Jin were then administering Shandong; they had earlier impeached Shoutong for failing to advance. When Taibuhua arrived, he dismissed them on the charge that they had failed to deliver supplies.

sentences.zh: 又以知樞密院事完者帖木兒為右丞之日嘗劾其非，亦加以失誤專制之罪，擅改其官，徵至軍欲害之。

translations.literal: He also, because Privy Council Vice-Director Qanisher Temür when he was Right Vice Chancellor had once impeached his wrongdoing, likewise imposed on him the crime of error and arbitrary control, changed his office on his own authority, summoned him to the army, and intended to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: He also punished Privy Council vice-director Qanisher Temür, who had impeached him when serving as right vice chancellor, charging him with misconduct and usurpation of authority, demoting him without authorization, summoning him to headquarters, and intending to kill him.

sentences.zh: 事聞，廷議喧然。

translations.literal: When the matter was heard, court discussion was in an uproar.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the capital, the court was in an uproar.

sentences.zh: 而太平與太不花久有隙，會其疏來上，以其欲害己也，遂諷監察御史迷只兒海等劾其緩師拒命之罪，而於帝前力譖之。

translations.literal: Taiping and Taibuhua had long had a rift. When his memorial came up, because Taiping believed Taibuhua wished to harm him, he thereupon prompted Supervising Censors Mizhihai and others to impeach him for the crimes of delaying the army and defying orders, and before the Emperor strongly slandered him.
translations.idiomatic: Taiping and Taibuhua had long been at odds. When the memorial arrived, Taiping, believing Taibuhua meant to kill him, prompted supervising censors including Mizhihai to charge him with delaying the campaign and defying orders, and vigorously denounced him before the emperor.

sentences.zh: 於是乃下詔削其官爵，奪其兵柄，安置於蓋州，以知樞密院事悟良哈台總其兵。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict was issued stripping his offices and titles, seizing his military authority, and placing him under restraint at Gaizhou, with Privy Council Vice-Director Uyangqatai taking overall command of his army.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then stripped him of rank and command, placed him under restraint at Gaizhou, and put Privy Council vice-director Uyangqatai in charge of his army.

sentences.zh: 太不花聞有詔，夜馳詣劉哈剌不花求救解。

translations.literal: When Taibuhua heard there was an edict, he galloped by night to Liu Qarabuq'a to beg rescue and release.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of the edict, Taibuhua rode through the night to Liu Qarabuq'a to beg for help.

sentences.zh: 劉哈剌不花者，太不花故部將也，以破賊累有功，拜淮南行省平章政事，時駐兵保定。

translations.literal: Liu Qarabuq'a was Taibuhua's former subordinate general. For repeatedly achieving merit in defeating bandits he was appointed Grand Councillor of the Huainan Branch Secretariat and was then encamped at Baoding.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qarabuq'a had been one of Taibuhua's generals and had won repeated distinction against the rebels. He was now grand councillor of the Huainan branch secretariat, with his troops at Baoding.

sentences.zh: 見太不花來，因張樂大宴，舉酒慷慨言曰：「丞相國家柱石，有大勳勞如此，天子終不害丞相，是必讒言間之耳。

translations.literal: Seeing Taibuhua come, he thereupon spread music and held a great feast, raised his cup and spoke with fervor, saying, "Chancellor, you are a pillar of the state. With such great merit and labor, the Son of Heaven in the end will not harm the Chancellor—this must surely be slander that has come between you.
translations.idiomatic: When Taibuhua arrived, Liu Qarabuq'a set out a feast with music and, raising his cup, spoke with feeling: "Chancellor, you are a pillar of the state. With merit such as yours, the Son of Heaven would never harm you—this can only be the work of slanderers.

sentences.zh: 我當自往見上言之，丞相毋憂也。」

translations.literal: I myself shall go to see the sovereign and speak on your behalf; Chancellor, do not worry."
translations.idiomatic: I will go to the emperor myself and plead your case—have no fear, Chancellor."

sentences.zh: 哈剌不花即走至京，首見太平。

translations.literal: Qarabuq'a at once ran to the capital and first saw Taiping.
translations.idiomatic: Qarabuq'a hurried to the capital and went first to Taiping.

sentences.zh: 太平問其來何故，哈剌不花具以其故告之。

translations.literal: Taiping asked why he had come; Qarabuq'a fully told him the reason.
translations.idiomatic: Taiping asked why he had come, and Qarabuq'a told him the whole story.

sentences.zh: 太平曰：「太不花大逆不道，今詔已下，爾乃敢輒妄言邪？

translations.literal: Taiping said, "Taibuhua is guilty of great rebellion and impiety. The edict has now been issued—how dare you presumptuously speak reckless words?
translations.idiomatic: Taiping said, "Taibuhua is guilty of treason. The edict has already been issued—how dare you speak on his behalf?

sentences.zh: 不審處，禍將及爾矣。」

translations.literal: If you do not consider your position carefully, calamity will reach you."
translations.idiomatic: If you do not watch your step, disaster will befall you as well."

sentences.zh: 哈剌不花聞太平言，畏懼，噤不能發。

translations.literal: When Qarabuq'a heard Taiping's words, he was afraid and dared not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Qarabuq'a was terrified by Taiping's words and fell silent.

sentences.zh: 太平度太不花必在哈剌不花所，即語之曰：「爾能致太不花以來，吾以爾見上，爾功不細矣。」

translations.literal: Taiping surmised that Taibuhua must be at Qarabuq'a's place and at once said to him, "If you can bring Taibuhua here, I will present you to the sovereign—your merit will not be slight."
translations.idiomatic: Taiping guessed that Taibuhua was hiding with Qarabuq'a and said, "If you can deliver Taibuhua to me, I will present you to the emperor—your reward will be great."

sentences.zh: 哈剌不花因許之。

translations.literal: Qarabuq'a thereupon promised.
translations.idiomatic: Qarabuq'a agreed.

sentences.zh: 太平乃引入見帝，賜賚良渥。

translations.literal: Taiping then introduced him to see the Emperor and bestowed rewards very generously.
translations.idiomatic: Taiping then presented him to the emperor, who lavished gifts upon him.

sentences.zh: 初，劉哈剌不花之為部將於太不花也，與倪晦者同在幕下，太不花每委任晦，而哈剌不花計多阻不行，哈剌不花心嘗以為怨。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Liu Qarabuq'a had been a subordinate general under Taibuhua, he and one Ni Hui had both been in the staff. Taibuhua always entrusted affairs to Hui, while Qarabuq'a's plans were often blocked and not carried out; Qarabuq'a in his heart had long harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Liu Qarabuq'a had served under Taibuhua, he and a staff officer named Ni Hui had shared the same command. Taibuhua favored Hui, while Qarabuq'a's counsel was repeatedly ignored, and he had long nursed a grudge.

sentences.zh: 及是，知事已不可解，還，縛太不花父子送京師，未至，皆殺之於路。

translations.literal: At this juncture, knowing the affair could no longer be resolved, he returned, bound Taibuhua and his son, and sent them to the capital. Before they arrived, he killed them all on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Now, seeing that nothing could be salvaged, he returned, bound Taibuhua and his son, and set out for the capital with them as prisoners. Before they arrived, he killed them both on the road.

sentences.zh: 察罕帖木兒 擴廓帖木兒

translations.literal: Chaghan Temur; Köke Temur
translations.idiomatic: Chaghan Temur; Köke Temur

sentences.zh: 察罕帖木兒，字廷瑞，係出北庭。

translations.literal: Chaghan Temur, styled Tingrui, was descended from the Northern Court.
translations.idiomatic: Chaghan Temur, courtesy name Tingrui, traced his lineage to the Northern Court.

sentences.zh: 曾祖闊闊台，元初隨大軍收河南。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Köködei, at the beginning of the Yuan, followed the great army in recovering Henan.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Köködei had followed the main armies in the conquest of Henan at the founding of the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 至祖乃蠻台、父阿魯溫，皆家河南，為潁州沈丘人。

translations.literal: Down to his grandfather Naimantai and his father Aruγun, all made their home in Henan and were natives of Shenqiu in Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Naimantai and his father Aruγun had both settled in Henan; the family were natives of Shenqiu in Ying prefecture.

sentences.zh: 察罕帖木兒幼篤學，嘗應進士舉，有時名。

translations.literal: Chaghan Temur in youth was devoted to learning; he once entered the jinshi examination and had a reputation in his time.
translations.idiomatic: Chaghan Temur studied diligently in his youth, once sat for the jinshi examination, and enjoyed a measure of renown.

sentences.zh: 身長七尺，修眉覆目，左頰有三毫，或怒則毫皆直指。

translations.literal: His body was seven chi in height; his long eyebrows covered his eyes. On his left cheek were three hairs, and when he was angry the hairs all pointed straight out.
translations.idiomatic: He stood seven chi tall, with long brows that shaded his eyes. Three hairs grew on his left cheek, and when he grew angry they bristled straight outward.

sentences.zh: 居常慨然有當世之志。

translations.literal: In daily life he would sigh with emotion, having the ambition to accomplish something in his age.
translations.idiomatic: He often spoke with feeling of his ambition to serve the age.

sentences.zh: 至正十一年，盜發汝、潁，焚城邑，殺長吏，所過殘破，不數月，江淮諸郡皆陷。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Zhizheng bandits rose in Ru and Ying, burned cities and towns, killed chief officials, and wherever they passed left ruin. Within a few months all the commanderies of the Jianghuai region fell.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Zhizheng (1351) rebels broke out in the Ru and Ying region, burning towns, killing officials, and laying waste wherever they marched. Within months the Jianghuai commanderies had all fallen.

sentences.zh: 朝廷徵兵致討，卒無成功。

translations.literal: The court raised troops to campaign against them, but in the end achieved no success.
translations.idiomatic: The court mobilized armies to suppress them but achieved nothing.

sentences.zh: 十二年，察罕帖木兒乃奮義起兵，沈丘之子弟從者數百人。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year Chaghan Temur then roused himself in righteous cause and raised troops; several hundred youths of Shenqiu followed him.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year (1352) Chaghan Temur raised a loyalist force of his own, and several hundred young men of Shenqiu rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 與信陽之羅山人李思齊合兵，同設奇計襲破羅山。

translations.literal: He joined forces with Li Siqi of Luoshan in Xinyang, and together they devised a stratagem and made a surprise attack that broke Luoshan.
translations.idiomatic: He joined forces with Li Siqi of Luoshan in Xinyang, and together they devised a stratagem that took Luoshan by surprise.

sentences.zh: 事聞，朝廷授察罕帖木兒中順大夫、汝寧府達魯花赤。

translations.literal: When the affair was reported, the court appointed Chaghan Temur Grand Master of Palace Attendance and Daruγači of Runing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, he was appointed grand master of palace attendance and daruγači of Runing prefecture.

sentences.zh: 於是所在義士俱將兵來會，得萬人，自成一軍，屯沈丘，數與賊戰，輒克捷。

translations.literal: Thereupon righteous men everywhere all led troops to assemble; he obtained ten thousand men, formed his own army, encamped at Shenqiu, and fought the bandits many times, always gaining victory.
translations.idiomatic: Loyalist volunteers from across the region flocked to him with their troops until he had ten thousand men under arms. He encamped at Shenqiu as an independent force and fought the rebels again and again, winning every engagement.

sentences.zh: 十五年，賊勢滋蔓，由汴以南陷鄧、許、嵩、洛。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year the bandits' momentum spread further; south of Bian they took Deng, Xu, Song, and Luo.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year (1355) the rebellion spread south of Bianliang, and Deng, Xu, Song, and Luo all fell.

sentences.zh: 察罕帖木兒兵日益盛，轉戰而北，遂戍虎牢，以遏賊鋒。

translations.literal: Chaghan Temur's army grew daily stronger. Turning to fight northward, he then garrisoned Hulao to check the bandits' spearhead.
translations.idiomatic: Chaghan Temur's army grew stronger by the day. Fighting his way north, he garrisoned Hulao to block the rebel advance.

sentences.zh: 賊乃北渡盟津，焚掠至覃懷，河北震動。

translations.literal: The bandits then crossed the Meng Ford northward, burning and plundering as far as Tanhuai; Hebei was shaken.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels crossed the Meng Ford northward, burning and looting as far as Tanhuai, and all of Hebei was thrown into alarm.

sentences.zh: 察罕帖木兒進戰，大敗之，餘黨柵河洲，殲之無遺類，河北遂定。

translations.literal: Chaghan Temur advanced to battle and greatly defeated them. The remnant band fortified themselves on the river islets; he annihilated them without survivors, and Hebei was then pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Chaghan Temur met them in battle and routed them utterly. The survivors fortified themselves on river islets, but he wiped them out to the last man, and Hebei was pacified.

sentences.zh: 朝廷奇其功，除中書刑部侍郎，階中議大夫。

translations.literal: The court marveled at his merit and appointed him Vice Minister of Punishments in the Central Secretariat, with the rank of Grand Master for Discussion.
translations.idiomatic: The court was astonished by his achievements and appointed him vice minister of punishments in the Central Secretariat, with the rank of grand master for discussion.

sentences.zh: 苗軍以滎陽叛，察罕帖木兒夜襲之，虜其眾幾盡，乃結營屯中牟。

translations.literal: The Miao army rebelled at Xingyang. Chaghan Temur made a night attack on them and captured nearly all their forces, then established a camp and encamped at Zhongmou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Miao army rebelled at Xingyang, Chaghan Temur attacked by night and captured nearly their entire force, then established a camp at Zhongmou.

sentences.zh: 已而淮右賊眾三十萬掠汴以西，來搗中牟營。

translations.literal: Before long three hundred thousand bandits of the Huaiyou region plundered west of Bian and came to strike at the Zhongmou camp.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward three hundred thousand Huaiyou rebels swept west of Bianliang and attacked his camp at Zhongmou.

sentences.zh: 察罕帖木兒結陳待之，以死生利害諭士卒。

translations.literal: Chaghan Temur formed battle lines to await them and instructed the soldiers on the gains and losses of life and death.
translations.idiomatic: Chaghan Temur drew up his battle line and addressed his men on the stakes of life and death.

sentences.zh: 士卒賈勇決死戰，無不一當百。

translations.literal: The soldiers summoned courage and resolved on a fight to the death; not one failed to match a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: His men took heart and fought as if each one were worth a hundred; none held back.

sentences.zh: 會大風揚沙，自率猛士鼓譟從中起，奮擊賊中堅，賊勢遂披靡不能支，棄旗鼓遁走，追殺十餘里，斬首無算。

translations.literal: It happened that a great wind raised sand. He himself led fierce warriors, beating drums and shouting, to rise from the center, fiercely striking the bandits' main force. The bandits' momentum then crumbled and they could not hold; they abandoned flags and drums and fled. He pursued and killed them for more than ten li, and the heads cut off were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: A fierce wind whipped up the sand. Chaghan Temur himself led his elite troops in a drum-beating charge at the enemy center. The rebel line collapsed; they threw down their banners and fled. He pursued them for more than ten li, and the slain were beyond count.

sentences.zh: 軍聲益大振。

translations.literal: The army's renown swelled still more.
translations.idiomatic: His army's fame grew still greater.

sentences.zh: 十六年，升中書兵部尚書，階嘉議大夫。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was promoted to Minister of War in the Central Secretariat, with the rank of Grand Master for Splendid Discussion.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year (1356) he was promoted to minister of war in the Central Secretariat, with the rank of grand master for splendid discussion.

sentences.zh: 繼而賊西陷陝州，斷殽、函，勢欲趨秦、晉。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward the bandits in the west took Shaanzhou, cutting Xiao and Han, with momentum intending to press toward Qin and Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the rebels in the west captured Shaanzhou, severing the Xiao and Han passes and threatening to advance into Shaanxi and Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 知樞密院事答失八都魯方節制河南軍，調察罕帖木兒與李思齊往攻之。

translations.literal: Privy Council Vice-Director Däshibadu'er was then controlling the Henan armies and dispatched Chaghan Temur and Li Siqi to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Privy Council vice-director Däshibadu'er, who then commanded the Henan armies, ordered Chaghan Temur and Li Siqi to attack them.

sentences.zh: 察罕帖木兒即鼓行而西，夜拔殽陵，立柵交口。

translations.literal: Chaghan Temur at once beat the drums and marched west, by night taking Xiaoling and establishing stockades at Jiaokou.
translations.idiomatic: Chaghan Temur marched west at once, took Xiaoling by night, and fortified Jiaokou.

sentences.zh: 陝為城，阻山帶河，險且固，而賊轉南山粟給食以堅守，攻之猝不可拔。

translations.literal: Shaan was a walled city, blocked by mountains and girded by rivers, perilous and firm, while the bandits transported grain from the southern mountains to supply food and held fast. An attack could not suddenly take it.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanzhou was a walled city, protected by mountains and rivers, formidable and well defended. The rebels hauled grain from the southern hills to sustain a long siege, and it could not be taken by assault.

sentences.zh: 察罕帖木兒乃焚馬矢營中，如炊煙狀，以疑賊，而夜提兵拔靈寶城。

translations.literal: Chaghan Temur then burned horse dung in the camp so that it resembled cooking smoke, to make the bandits suspicious, while by night he led troops and stormed Lingbao city.
translations.idiomatic: Chaghan Temur burned horse dung in camp to mimic cooking fires and deceive the enemy, then marched by night and stormed Lingbao.

sentences.zh: 守既備，賊始覺，不敢動，即渡河陷平陸，掠安邑，蹂晉南鄙。

translations.literal: When the defense was already prepared, the bandits only then realized it and did not dare move. They at once crossed the river, took Pinglu, plundered Anyi, and trampled the southern marches of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: By the time the garrison was ready, the rebels had only just realized what was happening and dared not stir. They crossed the river instead, seized Pinglu, looted Anyi, and ravaged southern Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 察罕帖木兒追襲之，蹙之以鐵騎。

translations.literal: Chaghan Temur pursued and struck them, pressing them with iron cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Chaghan Temur pursued them and harried them with his armored cavalry.

sentences.zh: 賊回扼下陽津，赴水死者甚眾。

translations.literal: The bandits turned back to hold Xiayang Ford; very many died entering the water.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels turned to hold Xiayang Ford, and great numbers drowned trying to cross the water.

sentences.zh: 相持數月，賊勢窮，皆遁潰。

translations.literal: They faced each other for several months until the bandits' momentum was exhausted and all fled in rout.
translations.idiomatic: After months of stalemate the rebels were exhausted and broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 以功加中奉大夫、僉河北行樞密院​​事。

translations.literal: For his merit he was given the additional rank of Grand Master for Court Discussion and made Concurrent Commissioner of the Hebei Branch Privy Council.
translations.idiomatic: For his achievements he was promoted to grand master for court discussion and appointed concurrent commissioner of the Hebei branch privy council.

sentences.zh: 十七年，賊尋出襄樊，陷商州，攻武關，官軍敗走，遂直趨長安，至灞上，分道掠同、華諸州，三輔震恐。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year the bandits soon emerged from Xiang and Fan, took Shangzhou, attacked Wuguan, and the government army was defeated and fled. They then pressed straight toward Chang'an, reaching Bashang, and in separate columns plundered Tong, Hua, and other prefectures. The Three Adjuncts were shaken with terror.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year (1357) the rebels emerged from Xiangyang, captured Shangzhou, and attacked Wuguan. The government troops were routed, and the rebels drove straight for Chang'an, reaching Bashang and raiding Tong, Hua, and neighboring prefectures in separate columns. The capital region was thrown into panic.

sentences.zh: 陝西省台來告急。

translations.literal: The Shaanxi provincial administration and surveillance commission came to report the emergency.
translations.idiomatic: The Shaanxi provincial and surveillance offices sent urgent appeals for help.

sentences.zh: 察罕帖木兒即領大眾入潼關，長驅而前，與賊遇，戰輒勝，殺獲以億萬計。

translations.literal: Chaghan Temur at once led a great host into Tong Pass and drove forward at full speed. Whenever he met the bandits in battle he won; those killed and captured were reckoned in the tens of millions.
translations.idiomatic: Chaghan Temur led a great army through Tong Pass and swept forward. In every encounter he was victorious, and the slain and captured were reckoned in the millions.

sentences.zh: 賊餘黨皆散潰，走南山，入興元。

translations.literal: The remnant bandits all scattered in rout, fled to the southern mountains, and entered Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The surviving rebels broke and fled south into the mountains and on into Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 朝廷嘉其復關陝有大功，授資善大夫、陝西行省左丞。

translations.literal: The court praised his great merit in recovering Guan and Shaan and appointed him Grand Master for Fostering Excellence and Left Vice Chancellor of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The court honored his great achievement in recovering the Guan-Shaan region and appointed him grand master for fostering excellence and left vice chancellor of the Shaanxi branch secretariat.

sentences.zh: 未幾，賊出自巴蜀，陷秦、隴，據鞏昌，遂窺鳳翔。

translations.literal: Before long bandits came out from Ba and Shu, took Qin and Long, held Gongchang, and then looked toward Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Before long rebels from Ba and Shu overran Qin and Long, seized Gongchang, and turned their eyes toward Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 察罕帖木兒即先分兵入守鳳翔城，而遣諜者誘賊圍鳳翔。

translations.literal: Chaghan Temur at once first divided troops to enter and defend Fengxiang city, while sending spies to lure the bandits to besiege Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Chaghan Temur first detached troops to hold Fengxiang, then sent agents to lure the rebels into besieging the city.

sentences.zh: 賊果來圍之，厚凡數十重。

translations.literal: The bandits indeed came to besiege it, their encirclement in depth numbering several tens of rings.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels came as expected and invested the city in dozens of concentric rings.

sentences.zh: 察罕帖木兒自將鐵騎，晝夜馳二百里往赴。

translations.literal: Chaghan Temur himself led iron cavalry, galloping day and night two hundred li to go to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Chaghan Temur himself led his armored cavalry on a forced march of two hundred li day and night.

sentences.zh: 比去城裡所，分軍張左右翼掩擊之。

translations.literal: When he was a li or so from the city, he divided the army, deployed left and right wings, and made a converging attack.
translations.idiomatic: When he was still a li from the city, he split his force and struck with both wings in a pincer movement.

sentences.zh: 城中軍亦開門鼓譟而出，內外合擊，呼聲動天地。

translations.literal: The troops in the city also opened the gates, beat drums and shouted, and came out. Inside and outside joined in the attack, and the cries shook heaven and earth.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison threw open the gates, drums beating, and charged out. Caught between the two forces, the rebels were crushed amid shouts that shook heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 賊大潰，自相踐蹂，斬首數万級，伏尸百餘里，餘黨皆遁還。

translations.literal: The bandits were greatly routed, trampling one another; heads cut off numbered tens of thousands, and corpses lay along the road for more than a hundred li. The remnant bandits all fled back.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels collapsed in utter rout, trampling one another underfoot. Tens of thousands were beheaded, and corpses littered the road for more than a hundred li. The survivors fled.

sentences.zh: 關中悉定。

translations.literal: All of Guanzhong was then pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The whole Guanzhong region was pacified.

sentences.zh: 十八年，山東賊分道犯京畿。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year the Shandong bandits in separate columns invaded the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year (1358) Shandong rebels advanced on the capital in several columns.

sentences.zh: 朝廷征四方兵入衛，詔察罕帖木兒以兵屯涿州。

translations.literal: The court summoned troops from the four directions to enter and guard the capital, and ordered Chaghan Temur to encamp his army at Zhuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: The court called up armies from every quarter to defend the capital and ordered Chaghan Temur to station his troops at Zhuozhou.

sentences.zh: 察罕帖木兒即留兵戍清湫、義谷，屯潼關，塞南山口，以備他盜。

translations.literal: Chaghan Temur at once left troops to garrison Qingqiu and Yigu, encamped at Tong Pass, and blocked the southern mountain passes to guard against other bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Chaghan Temur left troops to garrison Qingqiu and Yigu, stationed a force at Tong Pass, and sealed the southern mountain passes against other raiders.

sentences.zh: 而自將銳卒往赴召。

translations.literal: He himself led elite troops to answer the summons.
translations.idiomatic: He himself led his elite troops to answer the imperial summons.

sentences.zh: 而曹、濮賊方分道逾太行，焚上黨，掠晉、冀，陷雲中、雁門、代郡，烽火數千里，復大掠南且還。

translations.literal: Meanwhile the bandits of Cao and Pu were just then marching in separate columns over the Taihang range, burning Shangdang, plundering Jin and Ji, taking Yunzhong, Yanmen, and Dai commanderies. Beacon fires stretched for thousands of li, and they again plundered heavily to the south and were about to return.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile the Cao and Pu rebels were crossing the Taihang in separate columns, burning Shangdang, ravaging Shanxi and Hebei, and seizing Yunzhong, Yanmen, and Dai. Beacon fires blazed for a thousand li as they looted their way southward on the return march.

sentences.zh: 察罕帖木兒先遣兵伏南山阻隘，而自勒重兵屯聞喜、絳​​陽。

translations.literal: Chaghan Temur first sent troops to lie in ambush at the narrow passes of the southern mountains, while he himself drove heavy forces to encamp at Wenxi and Jiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Chaghan Temur first posted troops in ambush at the southern mountain defiles, then personally led his main force to Wenxi and Jiangyang.

sentences.zh: 賊果走南山，縱伏兵橫擊之，賊皆棄輜重走山谷，其得南還者無幾。

translations.literal: The bandits indeed fled along the southern mountains; he released the ambush troops to strike them across their line of march. The bandits all abandoned their baggage trains and fled into the valleys, and few who had gone south made it back south.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fled as expected along the southern route; he unleashed his ambush and cut them off. They abandoned their wagons and scattered into the hills, and scarcely any who had marched south returned alive.

sentences.zh: 乃分兵屯澤州，塞碗子城，屯上黨，塞吾兒谷，屯并州，塞井陘口，以杜太行諸道。

translations.literal: He then divided his troops to garrison Zezhou and block Wanzicheng, garrison Shangdang and block Wu'er Valley, garrison Bingzhou and block the Jingxing Pass, thereby sealing all routes through the Taihang.
translations.idiomatic: He then split his forces to hold Zezhou and seal Wanzicheng, Shangdang and Wu'er Valley, and Bingzhou and Jingxing Pass, shutting every road through the Taihang.

sentences.zh: 賊屢至，守將數血戰擊卻之，河東悉定。

translations.literal: The bandits came repeatedly, but the defending generals fought bloody battles time and again to beat them back, and Hedong was entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels attacked again and again, but the garrison commanders fought them off in repeated bloody engagements until all Hedong was pacified.

sentences.zh: 進陝西行省右丞，兼陝西行台侍御史、同知河南行樞密院事。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Right Councillor of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat, and concurrently served as attendant censor on the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat's surveillance commission and as associate commissioner of the Henan Branch Military Affairs Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to right councillor of the Shaanxi branch secretariat, and concurrently made attendant censor on the Shaanxi surveillance commission and associate commissioner of the Henan military affairs commission.

sentences.zh: 於是天子乃詔察罕帖木兒守禦關陝、晉、冀，撫鎮漢、沔、荊、襄，便宜行閫外事。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Son of Heaven issued an edict charging Chaghan Temur to defend the passes of Guanzhong and Shaanxi, Jin, and Ji, to pacify and garrison Han, Mian, Jing, and Xiang, and to conduct external military affairs at his discretion.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then ordered Chaghan Temur to defend Guanzhong, Shaanxi, Shanxi, and Hebei, to pacify Han, Mian, Jing, and Xiang, and to handle military affairs beyond the capital at his discretion.

sentences.zh: 察罕帖木兒益務練兵訓農，以平定四方為己責。

translations.literal: Chaghan Temur strove all the more to drill troops and train the farmers in agriculture, taking the pacification of the four quarters as his own responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: Chaghan Temur devoted himself ever more to drilling troops and training farmers, making the pacification of the realm his personal charge.

sentences.zh: 是年，安豐賊劉福通等陷汴梁，造宮闕，易正朔，號召群盜。

translations.literal: That year the Anfeng bandits Liu Futong and others took Bianliang, erected palace halls, changed the calendar, and summoned bands of robbers everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: That year Liu Futong and the other Anfeng rebels seized Bianliang, built palaces, proclaimed a new calendar, and called bandits to arms across the land.

sentences.zh: 巴蜀、荊楚、江淮、齊魯、遼海，西至甘肅，所在兵起，勢相聯結。

translations.literal: In Bashu, Jingchu, Jianghuai, Qilu, Liaohai, and west to Gansu, armies rose wherever one looked, their momentum interlinked.
translations.idiomatic: From Bashu, Jingchu, and the Jianghuai and Qilu regions to Liaohai and Gansu in the west, armies rose everywhere and their strength became interlinked.

sentences.zh: 察罕帖木兒乃北塞太行，南守鞏、洛，而自將中軍軍沔池。

translations.literal: Chaghan Temur sealed the Taihang to the north, held Gong and Luo to the south, and himself led the central army to encamp at Mianchi.
translations.idiomatic: Chaghan Temur blocked the Taihang to the north, held Gong and Luoyang to the south, and personally led the central army to camp at Mianchi.

sentences.zh: 會叛將周全棄覃懷，入汴城，合兵攻洛陽。

translations.literal: Just then the rebel general Zhou Quan abandoned Tanhuai, entered Bian City, and joined forces to attack Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the rebel general Zhou Quan abandoned Tanhuai, entered Bianliang, and joined the rebels in an assault on Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 察罕帖木兒下令嚴守備，別以奇兵出宜陽，而自將精騎發新安來援。

translations.literal: Chaghan Temur ordered strict defense, meanwhile sent a separate striking force out through Yiyang, and himself led elite cavalry from Xin'an to relieve the city.
translations.idiomatic: Chaghan Temur ordered the defenses tightened, sent a flanking force out through Yiyang, and himself led elite cavalry from Xin'an to relieve the city.

sentences.zh: 賊至城下，見堅壁不可犯，退引去，因追至虎牢，塞成皋諸險而還。

translations.literal: The bandits came beneath the walls, saw that the strong defenses could not be breached, withdrew and drew off, whereupon he pursued them to Hulao, sealed the passes of Chenggao and other strong points, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels reached the walls, found the defenses impregnable, and withdrew; he pursued them to Hulao, secured Chenggao and the other passes, and returned.

sentences.zh: 拜陝西行省平章政事，仍兼同知行樞密院事，便宜行事。

translations.literal: He was appointed Pingzhang of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat, still concurrently associate commissioner of the Branch Military Affairs Commission, with discretionary authority to act.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed pingzhang of the Shaanxi branch secretariat, retained his post as associate commissioner of the military affairs commission, and was granted discretionary authority.

sentences.zh: 十九年，察罕帖木兒圖复汴梁。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year Chaghan Temur planned to recover Bianliang.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year (1359) Chaghan Temur set out to recover Bianliang.

sentences.zh: 五月，以大軍次虎牢。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he brought a great army to camp at Hulao.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he advanced with a great army and encamped at Hulao.

sentences.zh: 先發遊騎，南道出汴南，略歸、亳、陳、察，北道出汴東，戰船浮於河，水陸並下，略曹南，據黃陵渡。

translations.literal: First he dispatched scouting cavalry: the southern route went out south of Bian, raiding Gui, Bo, Chen, and Cha; the northern route went out east of Bian, with warships floating on the river—land and water forces advancing together—raiding southern Cao and seizing Huangling Ford.
translations.idiomatic: He first sent out scouting cavalry: the southern column marched south of Bianliang and overran Gui, Bo, Chen, and Cha; the northern column marched east of Bianliang with warships on the river, advancing by land and water together to overrun southern Cao and seize Huangling Ford.

sentences.zh: 乃大發秦兵，出函關，過虎牢；

translations.literal: Then he greatly mobilized Qin troops, issuing through Hangu Pass and passing Hulao;
translations.idiomatic: He then mobilized the Qin armies in force, marching out through Hangu Pass and past Hulao;

sentences.zh: 晉兵出太行，逾黃河，俱會汴城下，首奪其外城。

translations.literal: Jin troops came out through the Taihang, crossed the Yellow River, and all assembled beneath Bian City, first seizing its outer walls.
translations.idiomatic: Shanxi troops came through the Taihang, crossed the Yellow River, and all converged beneath Bianliang, first taking the outer city.

sentences.zh: 察罕帖木兒自將鐵騎屯杏花營，諸將環城而壘。

translations.literal: Chaghan Temur himself led iron cavalry to encamp at Apricot Blossom Camp, while the generals ringed the city with fortified camps.
translations.idiomatic: Chaghan Temur himself led his armored cavalry to camp at Apricot Blossom Camp while his generals ringed the city with fortified camps.

sentences.zh: 賊屢出戰，戰輒敗，遂嬰城以守。

translations.literal: The bandits sallied repeatedly but were defeated in every battle, and finally clung to the walls for a stubborn defense.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels sallied again and again but were beaten every time, and at last shut themselves inside the walls.

sentences.zh: 乃夜伏兵城南，旦日，遣苗軍跳梁者略城而東。

translations.literal: He then hid troops by night south of the city; at daybreak he sent Miao troops who leaped and swaggered to mock-raid along the walls eastward.
translations.idiomatic: He hid troops south of the city by night; at dawn he sent Miao soldiers to swagger along the walls in a feint toward the east.

sentences.zh: 賊傾城出追，伏兵鼓譟起，邀擊敗之。

translations.literal: The bandits emptied the city in pursuit; the ambush troops beat drums and raised a clamor, intercepted them, and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels emptied the city in pursuit; the ambush rose with a thunder of drums, cut them off, and routed them.

sentences.zh: 又令弱卒立柵外城以餌賊。

translations.literal: He also ordered weak soldiers to erect a stockade outside the outer wall as bait for the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered weak troops to build a stockade outside the outer wall as bait for the enemy.

sentences.zh: 賊出爭之，弱卒佯走，薄城西，因突鐵騎縱擊，悉擒其眾。

translations.literal: The bandits came out to contest it; the weak soldiers feigned flight and drew close to the west of the city, whereupon iron cavalry burst out in a full charge and captured the whole force.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels came out to seize it; the weak troops feigned retreat and drew them to the west wall, where armored cavalry burst forth and captured them to the last man.

sentences.zh: 賊自是益不敢出。

translations.literal: From then on the bandits dared venture out even less.
translations.idiomatic: After that the rebels scarcely dared venture outside the walls at all.

sentences.zh: 八月，諜知城中計窮，食且盡，乃與諸將閆思孝、李克彝、虎林赤、賽因赤、答忽、脫因不花、呂文、完哲、賀宗哲、安童、張守禮、伯顏、孫翥、姚守德、魏賽因不花、楊履信、關關等議，各分門而攻。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, spies reported that stratagems within the city were exhausted and provisions were nearly gone; he thereupon consulted with the generals Yan Sixiao, Li Keyi, Hulinchi, Sayinchi, Dahu, Tuoyin Buhua, Lü Wen, Wanzhe, He Zongzhe, Antong, Zhang Shouli, Bayan, Sun Gao, Yao Shoude, Wei Sayin Buhua, Yang Lüxin, Guan Guan, and others, and they decided each to assault a separate gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month spies reported that the rebels' plans were exhausted and their food nearly gone; he consulted his generals Yan Sixiao, Li Keyi, Hulinchi, Sayinchi, Dahu, Tuoyin Buhua, Lü Wen, Wanzhe, He Zongzhe, Antong, Zhang Shouli, Bayan, Sun Gao, Yao Shoude, Wei Sayin Buhua, Yang Lüxin, Guan Guan, and others, and they agreed to assault each gate separately.

sentences.zh: 至夜，將士鼓勇登城，斬關而入，遂拔之。

translations.literal: When night came, officers and soldiers with drumming courage scaled the walls, cut through the gate bar and entered, and thus took the city.
translations.idiomatic: At nightfall the troops scaled the walls with beating drums, broke the gate bar, and stormed in; the city fell.

sentences.zh: 劉福通奉其偽主從數百騎出東門遁走。

translations.literal: Liu Futong escorted his false sovereign with several hundred horsemen out the east gate and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Futong escorted his puppet ruler with a few hundred horsemen out the east gate and fled.

sentences.zh: 獲偽後及賊妻子數万、偽官五千、符璽印章寶貨無算。

translations.literal: They captured the false empress and tens of thousands of bandit wives and children, five thousand false officials, seals and stamps, and treasure beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: They captured the rebel empress, tens of thousands of rebels' wives and children, five thousand puppet officials, seals and regalia, and treasure beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 全居民二十萬。

translations.literal: Two hundred thousand resident civilians were preserved intact.
translations.idiomatic: Two hundred thousand civilians were spared.

sentences.zh: 軍不敢私，市不易肆，不旬日河南悉定。

translations.literal: The army dared take nothing for private gain, markets did not alter their stalls, and within less than ten days all Henan was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The army took no private loot, the markets stayed open, and within ten days all Henan was pacified.

sentences.zh: 獻捷京師，歡聲動中外，以功拜河南行省平章政事，兼知河南行樞密院事、陝西行台御史中丞，仍便宜行事。

translations.literal: The victory was presented in the capital; shouts of joy moved court and country alike; for his merit he was appointed Pingzhang of the Henan Branch Secretariat, concurrently in charge of the Henan Branch Military Affairs Commission and surveillance censor-in-chief on the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat's commission, still with discretionary authority.
translations.idiomatic: News of the victory reached the capital and joy resounded through court and countryside; for his merit he was made pingzhang of the Henan branch secretariat, placed in charge of the Henan military affairs commission, and retained as Shaanxi surveillance censor-in-chief with discretionary authority.

sentences.zh: 詔告天下。

translations.literal: An edict announced this to all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: An edict proclaimed the victory to the realm.

sentences.zh: 先是，中原亂，江南海漕不復通，京師屢苦飢。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Central Plains were in turmoil, the Jiangnan sea transport of grain tribute ceased to reach the capital, and the imperial city suffered hunger repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, with the Central Plains in chaos, the Jiangnan grain convoys by sea had ceased, and the capital had suffered repeated famines.

sentences.zh: 至是，河南既定，檄書達江浙，海漕乃復至。

translations.literal: Now Henan was settled, dispatches reached Jiangsu and Zhejiang, and the sea transport of grain again arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Now that Henan was secure, his dispatches reached Jiangsu and Zhejiang, and the sea transport of grain resumed.

sentences.zh: 察罕帖木兒既定河南，乃以兵分鎮關陝、荊襄、河洛、江淮，而重兵屯太行，營壘旌旗相望數千里。

translations.literal: After Chaghan Temur had secured Henan, he divided troops to garrison the passes of Guanzhong and Shaanxi, Jing and Xiang, He and Luo, Jiang and Huai, while massing heavy forces on the Taihang—camps and banners visible to one another for thousands of li.
translations.idiomatic: Once Henan was secure, Chaghan Temur posted troops to garrison Guanzhong, Shaanxi, Jingxiang, the He-Luo region, and the Jianghuai, while massing his main force on the Taihang, where camps and banners stood within sight of one another for a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 乃日修車船，繕兵甲，務農積穀，訓練士卒，謀大舉以復山東。

translations.literal: He then daily repaired chariots and ships, mended armor and weapons, devoted himself to farming and storing grain, trained soldiers, and planned a great campaign to recover Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He repaired chariots and ships daily, refitted arms and armor, promoted farming and grain stores, drilled his troops, and planned a major campaign to recover Shandong.

sentences.zh: 先是，山西晉、冀之地皆察罕帖木兒所平定。

translations.literal: Earlier, the territories of Jin and Ji in Shanxi had all been pacified by Chaghan Temur.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Jin and Ji regions of Shanxi had all been pacified by Chaghan Temur.

sentences.zh: 而答失八都魯之子曰孛羅帖木兒，以兵駐大同，因欲並據晉、冀，遂至兵爭，天子屢下詔和解之，終不聽，事見《本紀》及《答失八都魯傳》中。

translations.literal: But Däshibadu'er's son, called Boluo Temur, held troops at Datong and wished thereby to seize Jin and Ji together, whereupon they came to armed conflict; the Son of Heaven repeatedly issued edicts to reconcile them, but in the end they would not obey—the affair is recorded in the Basic Annals and the biography of Däshibadu'er.
translations.idiomatic: But Däshibadu'er's son Boluo Temur held troops at Datong and sought to seize Shanxi and Hebei for himself, and they came to blows; the emperor repeatedly issued edicts to reconcile them, but they would not comply—the affair is recorded in the Basic Annals and the biography of Däshibadu'er.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，諜知山東群賊自相攻殺，而濟寧田豐降於賊。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, spies reported that the bands of robbers in Shandong were slaughtering one another, while Tian Feng of Jining had submitted to the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year (1361) spies reported that the rebel bands in Shandong were slaughtering one another, while Tian Feng of Jining had gone over to the rebels.

sentences.zh: 六月，察罕帖木兒乃輿疾自陝抵洛，大會諸將，與議師期。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Chaghan Temur, though carried in his litter because of illness, went from Shaanxi to Luoyang, held a great assembly of generals, and with them set the date for the army's march.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Chaghan Temur, though ill enough to travel by litter, went from Shaanxi to Luoyang, summoned his generals, and fixed the date for the campaign.

sentences.zh: 發并州軍出井陘，遼、沁軍出邯鄲，澤、潞軍出磁州，懷、衛軍出白馬，及汴、洛軍，水陸俱下，分道並進。

translations.literal: Troops from Bingzhou issued through Jingxing, Liao and Qin troops through Handan, Ze and Lu troops through Cizhou, Huai and Wei troops through Baima, together with the Bian and Luo armies—by water and land all advanced, marching in separate columns and converging.
translations.idiomatic: The Bingzhou army marched out through Jingxing, the Liao and Qin armies through Handan, the Ze and Lu armies through Cizhou, the Huai and Wei armies through Baima, together with the Bian and Luoyang forces—all advanced by land and water in separate columns and converged.

sentences.zh: 而自率鐵騎，建大將旗鼓，渡孟津，逾覃懷，鼓行而東，复冠州、東昌。

translations.literal: He himself led iron cavalry, raised the grand marshal's drums and banners, crossed Meng Ford, passed Tanhuai, marched east with beating drums, and recovered Guanzhou and Dongchang.
translations.idiomatic: He himself led his armored cavalry, raised the grand marshal's drums and banners, crossed Meng Ford, passed Tanhuai, marched east with beating drums, and recovered Guanzhou and Dongchang.

sentences.zh: 八月，師至鹽河。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the army reached the Salt River.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the army reached the Salt River.

sentences.zh: 遣其子擴廓帖木兒及諸將等，以精卒五萬搗東平。

translations.literal: He dispatched his son Köke Temur and other generals with fifty thousand picked troops to strike at Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his son Köke Temur and other generals with fifty thousand picked troops to strike Dongping.

sentences.zh: 與東平賊兵遇，兩戰皆敗之，斬首萬餘級，直抵其城下。

translations.literal: They encountered the Dongping bandit army, defeated them in two battles, beheaded more than ten thousand, and pressed straight to the walls of the city.
translations.idiomatic: They met the Dongping rebel army, defeated them in two battles, beheaded more than ten thousand, and pressed to the city walls.

sentences.zh: 察罕帖木兒以田豐據山東久，軍民服之，乃遣書諭以逆順之理。

translations.literal: Chaghan Temur, because Tian Feng had long held Shandong and troops and people obeyed him, sent a letter expounding the logic of rebellion and loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Because Tian Feng had long held Shandong and the troops and people obeyed him, Chaghan Temur sent a letter setting forth the logic of rebellion and loyalty.

sentences.zh: 豐及王士誠皆降。

translations.literal: Tian Feng and Wang Shicheng both submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Feng and Wang Shicheng both submitted.

sentences.zh: 遂復東平、濟寧。

translations.literal: He thereupon recovered Dongping and Jining.
translations.idiomatic: He then recovered Dongping and Jining.

sentences.zh: 時大軍猶未渡，群賊皆聚於濟南，而出兵齊河、禹城以相抗。

translations.literal: The main army had not yet crossed the river; the bandit hosts all gathered at Jinan, while sending troops to Qihe and Yucheng to resist.
translations.idiomatic: The main army had not yet crossed the river; the rebel hosts gathered at Jinan and sent troops to Qihe and Yucheng to resist.

sentences.zh: 察罕帖木兒分遣奇兵，取間道出賊後，南略泰安，逼益都，北徇濟陽、章丘，中循瀕海郡邑。

translations.literal: Chaghan Temur dispatched striking forces in separate columns, taking secret routes to emerge behind the bandits—south raiding Tai'an and pressing Yidu, north sweeping Jiyang and Zhangqiu, in the center marching along the coastal commanderies and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Chaghan Temur sent flanking columns by secret routes behind the enemy—south to overrun Tai'an and press Yidu, north to sweep Jiyang and Zhangqiu, and in the center along the coastal counties.

sentences.zh: 乃自將大軍渡河，與賊將戰於分齊，大敗之，進逼濟南城，而齊河、禹城俱來降，南道諸將亦報捷。

translations.literal: He then himself led the great army across the river, fought the bandit generals at Fenqi, routed them utterly, pressed close to Jinan City—and Qihe and Yucheng both came over to submit, while the southern route generals also reported victory.
translations.idiomatic: He then led the main army across the river, fought the rebel generals at Fenqi, routed them utterly, and pressed on Jinan; Qihe and Yucheng both submitted, and the southern columns also reported victory.

sentences.zh: 再敗益都兵於好石橋，東至海濱，郡邑聞風皆送款。

translations.literal: He again defeated the Yidu troops at Haoshi Bridge; east to the seashore, commanderies and counties at the news all offered their allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: He again defeated the Yidu troops at Haoshi Bridge; east to the seashore, counties and prefectures submitted at the news.

sentences.zh: 攻圍濟南三月，城乃下。

translations.literal: He besieged Jinan for three months before the city fell.
translations.idiomatic: He besieged Jinan for three months before the city fell.

sentences.zh: 詔拜中書平章政事、知河南山東行樞密院事，陝西行台中丞如故。

translations.literal: An edict appointed him Pingzhang of the Central Secretariat, in charge of the Henan-Shandong Branch Military Affairs Commission, with his post as Shaanxi surveillance censor unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed him pingzhang of the central secretariat and placed him in charge of the Henan-Shandong military affairs commission, while his post as Shaanxi surveillance censor remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 察罕帖木兒遂移兵圍益都，環城列營凡數十，大治攻具，百道並進。

translations.literal: Chaghan Temur then shifted his army to besiege Yidu, ringing the city with several dozen camps, greatly preparing siege engines, and advancing from a hundred directions at once.
translations.idiomatic: Chaghan Temur then shifted his army to besiege Yidu, ringed the city with several dozen camps, prepared siege engines on a great scale, and attacked from a hundred directions at once.

sentences.zh: 賊悉力拒守。

translations.literal: The bandits resisted with all their strength.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels resisted with all their strength.

sentences.zh: 复掘重塹，築長圍，遏南洋河以灌城中。

translations.literal: They again dug deep moats, built long encirclements, and dammed the Nanyang River to flood the city.
translations.idiomatic: They dug deep moats, built long siege lines, and dammed the Nanyang River to flood the city.

sentences.zh: 仍分守要害，收輯流亡，郡縣戶口再歸職方，號令煥然矣。

translations.literal: Meanwhile they posted garrisons at key points, gathered in the displaced, and county household registers again returned to the Board of Revenue—orders and regulations flourished once more.
translations.idiomatic: They also posted garrisons at key points, gathered in the displaced, and county household registers returned to the Board of Revenue; order and authority were restored.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，時山東俱平，獨益都孤城猶未下。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, when all Shandong was pacified, only the isolated city of Yidu had not yet fallen.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year (1362), when all Shandong was pacified, only the isolated city of Yidu still held out.

sentences.zh: 六月，田豐、王士誠陰結賊，复圖叛。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Tian Feng and Wang Shicheng secretly linked with the bandits and again plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Tian Feng and Wang Shicheng secretly conspired with the rebels and plotted rebellion again.

sentences.zh: 田豐之降也，察罕帖木兒推誠待之不疑，數獨入其帳中。

translations.literal: When Tian Feng had submitted, Chaghan Temur had treated him with open sincerity and never doubted him, often entering his tent alone.
translations.idiomatic: When Tian Feng had submitted, Chaghan Temur had treated him with complete trust and often entered his tent alone.

sentences.zh: 及豐既謀變，乃請察罕帖木兒行觀營壘。

translations.literal: Once Tian Feng had already plotted treachery, he invited Chaghan Temur to come inspect the camps.
translations.idiomatic: Once Tian Feng had plotted treachery, he invited Chaghan Temur to inspect the camps in person.

sentences.zh: 眾以為不可往，察罕帖木兒曰：「吾推心待人，安得人人而防之？」

translations.literal: Everyone held that he ought not go. Chaghan Temur said, "I treat others with an open heart—how can I guard against every single person one by one?"
translations.idiomatic: His officers urged him not to go. Chaghan Temur said, "I deal with people in good faith—must I suspect everyone?"

sentences.zh: 左右請以力士從，又不許，乃從輕騎十有一人行。

translations.literal: His attendants asked that strong men accompany him, but again he would not permit it, and went with only eleven light horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: When his attendants asked to send strong men along, he again refused and rode out with only eleven light horsemen.

sentences.zh: 至王信營，又至豐營，遂為王士誠所刺。

translations.literal: He reached Wang Xin's camp, then Tian Feng's camp, and there Wang Shicheng stabbed him.
translations.idiomatic: He reached Wang Xin's camp, then Tian Feng's camp, where Wang Shicheng stabbed him.

sentences.zh: 訃聞，帝震悼，朝廷公卿及京師四方之人，不問男女老幼，無不慟哭者。

translations.literal: When word of his death arrived, the emperor was shaken with grief; court nobles and officials and people of the capital and the four quarters, regardless of age or sex, none failed to wail in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When word of his death arrived, the emperor was stricken with grief; nobles, officials, and people of the capital and the four quarters, young and old, men and women alike, all wept in mourning.

sentences.zh: 先是，有白氣如索，長五百餘丈，起危宿，掃太微垣。

translations.literal: Earlier there had been a white vapor like a cord, more than five hundred zhang long, rising from the lodge Wei and sweeping through the celestial court of Taiwei.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier a white vapor like a cord, more than five hundred zhang long, had risen from the lodge Wei and swept across the celestial court of Taiwei.

sentences.zh: 太史奏山東當大水。

translations.literal: The court astronomers reported that Shandong would suffer great floods.
translations.idiomatic: The court astronomers reported that Shandong would suffer great floods.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「不然，山東必失一良將。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Not so—Shandong will certainly lose a fine general."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Not so—Shandong will surely lose a fine general."

sentences.zh: 即馳詔戒察罕帖木兒勿輕舉，未至而已及於難。

translations.literal: He immediately sent urgent edicts warning Chaghan Temur not to act rashly, but they arrived too late and disaster had already befallen him.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately sent urgent edicts warning Chaghan Temur not to act rashly, but they arrived too late and disaster had already befallen him.

sentences.zh: 詔贈推誠定遠宣忠亮節功臣、開府儀同三司、上柱國、河南行省左丞相，追封忠襄王，諡獻武。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously granted him the title Meritorious Minister of Sincere Loyalty, Far-reaching Stabilization, Manifest Loyalty, and Bright Integrity; Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with authority equal to the Three Excellencies; Supreme Pillar of State; Left Chancellor of the Henan Branch Secretariat; posthumously enfeoffed as Prince Loyal-Assistance with the posthumous epithet Martial-Exemplar.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously granted him the title of meritorious minister of sincere loyalty and far-reaching stabilization, made him grand master of splendid happiness with authority equal to the Three Excellencies and supreme pillar of state, appointed him left chancellor of the Henan branch secretariat, and enfeoffed him posthumously as Prince Loyal-Assistance with the epithet Martial-Exemplar.

sentences.zh: 及葬，賜賻有加，改贈宣忠興運弘仁效節功臣，追封潁川王，改諡忠襄，食邑沈丘縣，所在立祠，歲時致祭。

translations.literal: At his burial additional funeral gifts were bestowed; the grant was changed to Meritorious Minister of Manifest Loyalty, Rising Fortune, Broad Benevolence, and Effective Integrity; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Yingchuan and the epithet changed to Loyal-Assistance; his fief was Shenqiu County; temples were erected wherever he had served and sacrifices offered at the seasons.
translations.idiomatic: At his burial additional funeral gifts were bestowed; his title was changed to meritorious minister of manifest loyalty, rising fortune, broad benevolence, and effective integrity; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Yingchuan with the epithet Loyal-Assistance; his fief was Shenqiu County; temples were erected wherever he had served and seasonal sacrifices offered.

sentences.zh: 封其父阿魯溫汝陽王，後又進封梁王。

translations.literal: His father Aru Temur was enfeoffed as Prince of Ruyang, later advanced to Prince of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Aru Temur was enfeoffed as Prince of Ruyang and later advanced to Prince of Liang.

sentences.zh: 於是復起擴廓帖木兒，拜銀青榮祿大夫、太尉、中書平章政事、知樞密院事、皇太子詹事，仍便宜行事，襲總其父兵。

translations.literal: Thereupon Köke Temur was raised up again, appointed Silver-Clad Blue Grand Mentor of Splendid Happiness, Grand Marshal, Pingzhang of the Central Secretariat, in charge of the Military Affairs Commission, Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent—with discretionary authority still—and inherited overall command of his father's armies.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Köke Temur was restored to office, appointed silver-clad blue grand mentor of splendid happiness, grand marshal, pingzhang of the central secretariat, placed in charge of the military affairs commission, and made grand mentor of the heir apparent, with discretionary authority and overall command of his father's armies.

sentences.zh: 擴廓帖木兒既領兵柄，銜哀以討賊，攻城益急，而城守益固，乃穴地通道以入。

translations.literal: Köke Temur, once he held the military command, carried grief in his heart as he attacked the bandits; the siege grew fiercer while the city's defense grew stouter, so he tunneled underground passages to enter.
translations.idiomatic: Once Köke Temur held military command, he attacked the rebels in grief for his father; the siege grew fiercer while the defense grew stouter, so he tunneled underground passages into the city.

sentences.zh: 十一月，拔其城，執其渠魁陳猱頭二百餘人獻闕下，而取田豐、王士誠之心以祭其父，餘黨皆就誅。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he took the city, seized more than two hundred ringleaders including Chen Maotou and presented them at court, took the hearts of Tian Feng and Wang Shicheng to sacrifice to his father, and the remaining partisans were all executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he took the city, seized more than two hundred ringleaders including Chen Maotou and presented them at court, took the hearts of Tian Feng and Wang Shicheng to sacrifice to his father, and executed the remaining partisans.

sentences.zh: 即遣關保以兵取莒州，於是山東悉平。

translations.literal: He immediately dispatched Guan Bao with troops to take Juzhou, and thus all Shandong was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately sent Guan Bao with troops to take Juzhou, and thus all Shandong was pacified.

sentences.zh: 擴廓帖木兒本察罕帖木兒之甥，自幼養以為子。

translations.literal: Köke Temur was in origin Chaghan Temur's nephew, reared from childhood and adopted as his son.
translations.idiomatic: Köke Temur was in fact Chaghan Temur's nephew, reared from childhood and adopted as his son.

sentences.zh: 當是時，東至淄、沂，西逾關陝，皆晏然無事。

translations.literal: At that time, east to Zi and Yi, west beyond the passes of Guanzhong and Shaanxi, all was tranquil and without incident.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, from Zi and Yi in the east to beyond Guanzhong and Shaanxi in the west, all was tranquil.

sentences.zh: 擴廓帖木兒乃駐兵於汴、洛。

translations.literal: Köke Temur then stationed troops at Bian and Luo.
translations.idiomatic: Köke Temur then stationed his troops at Bianliang and Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 朝廷方倚之以為安。

translations.literal: The court was just then relying on him for security.
translations.idiomatic: The court was just then relying on him for security.

sentences.zh: 孛羅帖木兒自察罕帖木兒既沒，復數以兵爭晉、冀。

translations.literal: After Chaghan Temur's death Boluo Temur again repeatedly contested Jin and Ji by force of arms.
translations.idiomatic: After Chaghan Temur's death Boluo Temur again repeatedly fought for control of Shanxi and Hebei.

sentences.zh: 帝雖屢解諭之，而仇隙日深。

translations.literal: Though the emperor repeatedly sent reconciliations, their enmity deepened daily.
translations.idiomatic: Though the emperor repeatedly urged reconciliation, their enmity deepened daily.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，御史大夫老的沙與知樞密院事禿堅帖木兒得罪於皇太子，皇太子欲誅之，皆奔於大同，為孛羅帖木兒所匿。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year the Censor-in-Chief Laodisha and the commissioner in charge of the Military Affairs Commission Tuqian Temur offended the Heir Apparent; the Heir Apparent wished to execute them, and both fled to Datong, where Boluo Temur concealed them.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year (1363) the censor-in-chief Laodisha and the military affairs commissioner Tuqian Temur offended the heir apparent, who wished to execute them; both fled to Datong, where Boluo Temur sheltered them.

sentences.zh: 老的沙者，帝母舅，以故帝數為皇太子寢其事，而皇太子不從，帝無如之何，則傳旨密令孛羅帖木兒隱其跡。

translations.literal: Laodisha was the emperor's maternal uncle; for this reason the emperor repeatedly urged the Heir Apparent to let the matter rest, but the Heir Apparent would not comply; the emperor could do nothing, and sent secret orders instructing Boluo Temur to hide their tracks.
translations.idiomatic: Laodisha was the emperor's maternal uncle; for this reason the emperor repeatedly urged the heir apparent to drop the matter, but the heir apparent would not comply; unable to act openly, the emperor sent secret orders instructing Boluo Temur to conceal them.

sentences.zh: 而丞相搠思監、宦者樸不花皆附皇太子，必窮竟其事。

translations.literal: But the Chancellor Suosijian and the eunuch Pak Buha both sided with the Heir Apparent and were determined to investigate the affair to its end.
translations.idiomatic: But the chancellor Suosijian and the eunuch Pak Buha both sided with the heir apparent and were determined to pursue the case to its end.

sentences.zh: 皇太子又方倚重於擴廓帖木兒。

translations.literal: The Heir Apparent was at the same time placing great reliance on Köke Temur.
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent was at the same time placing great reliance on Köke Temur.

sentences.zh: 時擴廓帖木兒駐太原，與孛羅帖木兒構兵，勢相持不可解。

translations.literal: At that time Köke Temur was stationed at Taiyuan and had taken up arms against Boluo Temur; their forces stood in stalemate and could not be resolved.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Köke Temur was stationed at Taiyuan and clashed with Boluo Temur; their forces were locked in stalemate with no resolution in sight.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，搠思監、樸不花因誣孛羅帖木兒、老的沙謀為不軌，而皇太子亦怒不已。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year Suosijian and Pak Buha falsely charged Boluo Temur and Laodisha with plotting sedition, and the Heir Apparent's anger did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year (1364) Suosijian and Pak Buha falsely charged Boluo Temur and Laodisha with plotting sedition, and the heir apparent's anger did not abate.

sentences.zh: 三月，天子以故下詔數孛羅帖木兒罪，削其官職而奪其兵。

translations.literal: In the third month the Son of Heaven for this reason issued an edict enumerating Boluo Temur's crimes, stripped him of his offices, and seized his troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the emperor issued an edict enumerating Boluo Temur's crimes, stripped him of his offices, and seized his troops.

sentences.zh: 孛羅帖木兒不受詔，遂遣兵逼京師，必欲得搠思監、樸不花乃已。

translations.literal: Boluo Temur did not accept the edict and thereupon sent troops to press the capital, determined not to stop until he had obtained Suosijian and Pak Buha.
translations.idiomatic: Boluo Temur refused the edict and sent troops against the capital, vowing not to stop until he had Suosijian and Pak Buha in his hands.

sentences.zh: 天子不得已，縛兩人與之。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven had no choice and bound the two men and handed them over.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had no choice and had the two men bound and handed over.

sentences.zh: 語在搠思監、孛羅帖木兒傳。

translations.literal: The account is given in the biographies of Suosijian and Boluo Temur.
translations.idiomatic: The full account is given in the biographies of Suosijian and Boluo Temur.

sentences.zh: 七月，孛羅帖木兒又與老的沙合禿堅帖木兒兵同犯闕。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Boluo Temur again joined Laodisha and Tuqian Temur's troops in assaulting the imperial precincts.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Boluo Temur again joined Laodisha and Tuqian Temur in marching on the capital.

sentences.zh: 時擴廓帖木兒遣部將白鎖住以萬騎衛京師，駐於龍虎台，與戰不利，遂奉皇太子奔於太原。

translations.literal: At that time Köke Temur had dispatched his subordinate general Bai Suozhu with ten thousand horsemen to guard the capital, encamped at Longhu Terrace; the battle went ill, and he thereupon escorted the Heir Apparent in flight to Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Köke Temur had sent his subordinate Bai Suozhu with ten thousand horsemen to guard the capital, encamped at Longhu Terrace; the battle went against them, and he escorted the heir apparent in flight to Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 孛羅帖木兒既入朝，據相位。

translations.literal: Boluo Temur, having entered court, seized the chancellorship.
translations.idiomatic: Once Boluo Temur had entered court, he seized the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 白鎖住又將二萬騎屯漁陽，為朝廷聲援。

translations.literal: Bai Suozhu again led twenty thousand horsemen to encamp at Yuyang as reinforcement for the court.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Suozhu again led twenty thousand horsemen to camp at Yuyang as a reinforcement for the court.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，擴廓帖木兒以兵搗大同取之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year Köke Temur struck at Datong with troops and took it.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year (1365) Köke Temur struck at Datong with troops and took it.

sentences.zh: 皇太子乃趣擴廓帖木兒大舉以討逆，發丞相也速兵屯東鄙，魏、遼、齊、吳、豫、豳諸王兵駐西邊，而自率擴廓帖木兒兵取中道，抵京師。

translations.literal: The heir apparent then urged Köke Temur to mount a great campaign against the rebels, mobilized Chancellor Yesüder's troops to the eastern frontier, posted the princes of Wei, Liao, Qi, Wu, Yu, and Bin on the western flank, and himself led Köke Temur's army by the central route to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent then urged Köke Temur to mount a great campaign against the rebels, mobilized Chancellor Yesüder's troops on the eastern frontier, posted the princes of Wei, Liao, Qi, Wu, Yu, and Bin on the west, and himself led Köke Temur's army by the central route to the capital.

sentences.zh: 亡何，孛羅帖木兒既伏誅，帝詔白鎖住兵守京城，遂詔皇太子還京，而擴廓帖木兒亦扈從入朝。

translations.literal: Before long Boluo Temur had been executed; the emperor ordered Bai Suozhu's troops to guard the capital, then summoned the heir apparent to return to the capital, and Köke Temur also escorted him into court.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Boluo Temur was executed; the emperor ordered Bai Suozhu's troops to guard the capital, summoned the heir apparent back to the capital, and Köke Temur escorted him into court.

sentences.zh: 九月，詔拜伯撒里右丞相，擴廓帖木兒左丞相。

translations.literal: In the ninth month an edict appointed Barsari right chancellor and Köke Temur left chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month an edict appointed Barsari right chancellor and Köke Temur left chancellor.

sentences.zh: 伯撒里累朝舊臣，而擴廓帖木兒以後生晚出，乃與並相。

translations.literal: Barsari was a veteran of many reigns, while Köke Temur was a younger man who had risen late, yet they were made coequal chancellors.
